issue.title: ace/restore.py shells out to sase stitch create with an unsupported positional NAME argument
issue.description: src/sase/ace/restore.py:220 calls run_workspace_command with ["sase", "stitch", "create", base_name] (was ["sase", "commit", base_name] before the stitch_create_migration plan renamed the CLI), but neither the sase commit legacy alias nor sase stitch create define a positional argument in src/sase/main/parser_commit.py's add_commit_create_options. That call therefore fails with argparse 'unrecognized arguments: <base_name>' and restore_patch reports the failure, breaking sase restore end-to-end. The same invalid form is documented (and now preserved verbatim, per the migration plan's explicit non-goal against opportunistic fixes) in docs/vcs.md as 'SASE_VCS_PROVIDER=git sase stitch create my_feature'. The likely intended fix is to pass the name via -n/--name (add_commit_create_options already defines -n/--name: 'Branch/Patch name (required for create_pull_request)') at both call sites, or to add a positional NAME argument to the parser if that is the intended UX. This is a pre-existing bug (predates the CLI rename), discovered and deliberately left unfixed while implementing sase/repos/plans/202608/stitch_create_migration.md's explicit follow-up-bead instruction.
